'''Piers Richard Corbyn''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|k|ɔː|ɹ|b|ɪ|n}}; born 10 March 1947)<ref name="Wired" /> is a British [[weather forecaster]], [[Anti-vaccine activism|anti-vaccine]] activist, [[Conspiracy theory|conspiracy theorist]], and former politician.{{refn|group=n|For the conspiracy theorist descriptor, see:
* [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-52674949 Glastonbury 5G report 'hijacked by conspiracy theorists']. BBC News.
* [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/coronavirus-anti-lockdown-protest-trafalgar-square-anti-vaccine-mask-hoax-a9695561.html Anti-lockdown, anti-vaccine and anti-mask protesters crowd London's Trafalgar Square]. ''The Independent''.
* [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/coronavirus-protests-hyde-park-london-jeremy-corbyn-piers-brother-lockdown-a9518341.html Coronavirus protests: Jeremy Corbyn's brother among protesters arrested at Hyde Park 'mass gathering']. ''The Independent''.
* [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/06/20/piers-corbyn-charged-breaching-lockdown-rules-two-occasions/ Piers Corbyn charged with breaching lockdown rules on two occasions]. ''The Daily Telegraph''.
* [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/men/thinking-man/covid-protests-climate-denial-family-nightmare-jeremy-corbyns/ Who is Jeremy Corbyn's brother Piers? Mask protests, climate denial and support for a no-deal Brexit]. ''The Daily Telegraph''}} Corbyn was born in [[Wiltshire]] and raised in [[Shropshire]] wherein he attended [[Adams' Grammar School]]. He was awarded a first class BSc degree in physics from [[Imperial College London]] in 1968 and a [[Postgraduate education|postgraduate]] [[Master of Science|MSc]] in [[astrophysics]] from [[Queen Mary University of London|Queen Mary College, University of London]], in 1981. Corbyn was a member of the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] and served as a councillor in the [[London Borough of Southwark]] from 1986 to 1990. He is the elder brother of former Labour Party leader [[Jeremy Corbyn]], leaving Labour in 2003 due to his opposition to the [[Iraq War]].

Corbyn ran a weather monitoring company called WeatherAction in the 1990s and gained some prominence in the media for his predictions and, later more so, for his [[Climate change denial|rejection]] of the [[scientific consensus on climate change]].

Throughout the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 pandemic]], he was a prominent proponent of [[COVID-19 misinformation|conspiracy theories]]. He described [[SARS-CoV-2]] as a "hoax", frequently campaigned against [[COVID-19 lockdowns#England|lockdowns]] and [[COVID-19 vaccine misinformation and hesitancy|against COVID-19 vaccines]], and described [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s as dangerous. Corbyn was arrested on several occasions for taking part in [[COVID-19 protests in the United Kingdom|protests against public health laws]], and on suspicion of encouraging people to burn down the offices of members of [[Parliament of the United Kingdom|Parliament]].<ref name=":0" />

== Early life and education ==
Piers Corbyn was born on 10 March 1947 in [[Chippenham]], Wiltshire.<ref name="Wired">{{cite news|last=Standage|first=Tom |author-link=Tom Standage|url=https://www.wired.com/1999/02/weather-2/|url-status=live|title=Everyone Complains About the Weather... Piers Corbyn Is Doing Something About It|magazine=Wired|date=1 February 1999|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104104415/http://www.wired.com/wired/archive/7.02/weather.html|archive-date=4 November 2012}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Trim|first1=Liam|last2=Colwill|first2=Jack|date=3 May 2020|title=5 dangerous virus claims made by anti-lockdown protests debunked|url=https://www.somersetlive.co.uk/news/somerset-news/coronavirus-myths-piers-corbyn-lockdown-4098881|access-date=28 September 2020|website=SomersetLive|archive-date=28 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201028194523/https://www.somersetlive.co.uk/news/somerset-news/coronavirus-myths-piers-corbyn-lockdown-4098881|url-status=live}}</ref> He grew up at Yew Tree Manor in [[Pave Lane]], in [[Newport, Shropshire]], a 17th-century [[English country house|country house]] which was once part of the [[Duke of Sutherland]]'s [[Lilleshall Hall|Lilleshall]] estate.<ref name="BurgessSale">{{cite news |last1=Burgess |first1=Kaya|title=Corbyn's family mansion for sale|url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/corbyn-s-family-mansion-for-sale-cz99j8ck3|access-date=27 August 2018|work=The Times|date=5 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211220620/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/corbyn-s-family-mansion-for-sale-cz99j8ck3|archive-date=11 December 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last2=Sawyer|first2=Patrick|last1=Ross|first1=Tim|title=Labour Turns Left: How the outsider with two grade Es at A-level became a prime minister in waiting|url=http://www.pressreader.com/uk/the-sunday-telegraph/20150913/281715498398812/TextView|work=[[The Sunday Telegraph]]|date=13 September 2015|access-date=17 December 2016|via=Press Reader|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002164535/http://www.pressreader.com/uk/the-sunday-telegraph/20150913/281715498398812/TextView|archive-date=2 October 2015}}</ref>
He began recording weather and [[climate pattern]]s in 1962 at the age of fifteen, constructing his own observation equipment.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.wired.com/1999/02/weather-2/ |magazine=wired |title=Everyone Complains About the Weather... Piers Corbyn Is Doing Something About It. |author=Tom Standage |date=1 February 1999 |access-date=12 March 2023}}</ref> He attended [[Castle House School]] and [[Adams' Grammar School]] in Newport, Shropshire. 

=== Higher education ===
At 18, he went to [[Imperial College London]],<ref name="Wired" /> being awarded a first class BSc degree in physics in 1968.<ref>[http://www.larouchepub.com/other/interviews/2007/3422piers_corbyn.html INTERVIEW: PIERS CORBYN] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305014337/http://www.larouchepub.com/other/interviews/2007/3422piers_corbyn.html |date=5 March 2016}} 1 June 2007 issue of Executive Intelligence Review.</ref> He commenced postgraduate research there into superconductivity, but then went into student representation and politics for some years. In 1979, he returned to postgraduate study at [[Queen Mary University of London|Queen Mary College, University of London]], being awarded an MSc in [[astrophysics]] in 1981.<ref>[http://www.qmul.ac.uk/alumni/pdfs/28553.pdf Whether the weather be...] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208124551/http://www.qmul.ac.uk/alumni/pdfs/28553.pdf |date=8 December 2015}} QUAD Magazine, 2007, Queen Mary University of London</ref> While he was an undergraduate, an article by Corbyn was published in the [[Royal Meteorological Society]]'s magazine ''Weather'' discussing a brine barometer and an electrical thermometer.<ref name="Wired" />

=== Student representative ===
In 1969, Corbyn became the first president of the [[Imperial College Union|Imperial College Students' Union]] to be directly elected by the student body. As president until 1970, Corbyn was successful in establishing a sabbatical union president, enabling the elected student leader to be registered at the college without having to study or pay fees (in fact they received a grant from the college and union).<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=x4u4ikoj1M8C&dq=piers+corbyn&pg=RA1-PA437 The History of Imperial College London, 1907–2007], Hannah Gay, p. 437</ref>

Corbyn set up a short-lived Imperial College Representative Council, seats on which were distributed between members of the college on the basis of their numbers, a system that almost gave students a majority. The ICAUT, a staff union, refused to cooperate with this student-led initiative. Although this particular council did not survive, increased student representation on college boards and committees became a lasting success of Corbyn's time as ICU president.{{citation needed|date=January 2025}}

Corbyn, together with the rector at the time, [[William George Penney, Baron Penney|Lord Penney]], received the Queen when she opened a new administrative building in 1969. During the visit Corbyn petitioned the Queen in front of 900 people, asking for students to be given greater say in the governance of the college.<ref>Gay, Hannah (2007). The History of Imperial College London, 1907–2007. London: Imperial College Press, 437, 477 and Illustration 102. {{ISBN|978-1-86094-708-7}}.</ref>

== Career ==

=== Housing-rights activist ===
Corbyn was a housing and [[Squatting in England and Wales|squatters' rights]] activist in the north [[Paddington]] area of the [[City of Westminster]] in the mid-1970s. He helped organise the All London Squatters Federation, the [[squatters union]] and the Squatters Action Council (SAC).<ref>{{Cite book |last=Vasudevan |first=Alexander |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y_qmDAAAQBAJ&dq=%22squatters+union%22&pg=PT63 |title=The Autonomous City: A History of Urban Squatting |date=16 May 2017 |publisher=Verso Books |isbn=9781781687871 |via=Google Books}}</ref> Although they issued publications and mounted protests, in the assessment of the [[Special Branch (Metropolitan Police)|Metropolitan Police Special Branch]] the "real activists" in these organisations, Corbyn among them, were "limited to not more than about a dozen persons" and had "very little influence on squatters".<ref>{{Cite book |last=Deputy Assistant Commissioner |first=Metropolitan Police, Special Branch |url=https://www.ucpi.org.uk/publications/special-branch-report-providing-an-assessment-of-squatting-in-london/ |title=Special Report: Squatting |date=12 August 1976 |publisher=Undercover Policing Inquiry, 2021 |year=}}</ref>  

In [[1974 Westminster City Council election|1974]], he stood for election to [[Westminster City Council]] in [[Harrow Road (ward)|Harrow Road]] ward as a Squatters and Tenants candidate; in [[1978 Westminster City Council election|1978]], he and a colleague stood in Harrow Road as Decent Housing candidates.<ref name="WCC election">[http://www.election.demon.co.uk/wcc/har.html Harrow Road ward] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070820141146/http://www.election.demon.co.uk/wcc/har.html |date=20 August 2007 }} election results</ref> In the [[1977 Greater London Council election|1977 GLC election]] he was the [[International Marxist Group]] candidate for [[Lambeth Central (electoral division)|Lambeth Central]].<ref name="GLC">{{cite web|url=http://www.election.demon.co.uk/glc/glclm.html|title=Greater London Council Election results: Lambeth|access-date=14 March 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061004071214/http://www.election.demon.co.uk/glc/glclm.html|archive-date=4 October 2006|url-status=live}}</ref> 

He and some of the squatters in [[Elgin Avenue]] were, as a result of their campaign which included the building of barricades against eviction, rehoused by the GLC in 1975 spread out between Westminster and other London boroughs to discourage the risk of further united action. For their 3-year occupation, it was "a 'victory' of sorts",<ref>{{Cite web |title=Community Politics: The Still Living Dead {{!}} libcom.org |url=https://libcom.org/article/community-politics-still-living-dead |access-date=31 May 2025 |website=libcom.org |language=en}}</ref> which Corbyn, attributed to three factors: (1) a public campaign that "related to the whole housing crisis" so that support was won from the labour movement; (2) democratic organisation so that "everyone could join in and know that what they did was part of what everyone was doing"; and (3) a readiness to "defy the law" proving that the residents were "serious and not squatting for fun".<ref name="Book262">{{cite book |last=Corbyn |first=Piers |url=https://en.squat.net/wp-content/uploads/en/2013/01/wates-wolmar-squatting-real-story.pdf |title=Squatting: The real story |date=1980 |publisher=Bay Leaf Books |isbn=0-9507259-1-9 |editor1-last=Wates |editor1-first=Nick |location=London |pages=141 |chapter=We won, you should fight them too |editor2-last=Wolmar |editor2-first=Christian}}</ref>

In August 1978, Corbyn, then with the Advisory Service for Squatters (ASS), was present when 650 members of the [[Special Patrol Group]] cleared 160 squatters out of 5 blocks in [[Huntley Street]], behind [[University College Hospital]].<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j9r6ac7RGS8 |title=SYND 16 8 78 SQUATTERS EVICTED BY THE POLICE IN LONDON |date=24 July 2015 |last=AP Archive |access-date=30 May 2025 |via=YouTube}}</ref><ref name="Kearns1979">{{cite journal |last1=Kearns |first1=Kevin C. |date=1979 |title=Intraurban Squatting in London |url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/2563131 |journal=Annals of the Association of American Geographers |volume=69 |issue=4 |pages=589–598 |doi=10.1111/j.1467-8306.1979.tb01284.x |issn=0004-5608 |jstor=2563131 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Corbyn summarised the squatters case in the slogan "No [housing] waiting lists while homes lie empty".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Huntley Street squatters outside court to defend... 04 Dec… |url=https://www.reportdigital.co.uk/reportage-photo-huntley-street-squatters-outside-court-to-defend--04-dec-1978-nla-photojournalism-image00105777.html |access-date=30 May 2025 |website=Report digital |language=en-UK}}</ref> With Jim Paton of the ASS, he was convicted of  "resisting the sheriff" contrary to Section 10 of the [[Criminal Law Act 1977]]. In solidarity, 150 [[Squatting in the Netherlands|Dutch squatters]] "besieged" at the British Embassy in [[The Hague]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=16 August 2018 |title=Today in London squatting history, 1978: mass eviction in Huntley Street, Bloomsbury. |url=https://pasttense.co.uk/2018/08/16/today-in-london-squatting-history-1978-mass-eviction-in-huntley-street-bloomsbury/ |access-date=30 May 2025 |website=LONDON RADICAL HISTORIES |language=en}}</ref>

=== Party politics ===
Corbyn was a member of the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]]. He was elected as a Labour councillor for Burgess Ward of the [[Southwark London Borough Council]] in [[1986 Southwark London Borough Council election|1986]] but lost in [[1990 Southwark London Borough Council election|1990]].<ref>[http://www.london-se1.co.uk/news/view/8181 Ex-Labour councillor Piers Corbyn to stand in Chaucer by-election] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150910090101/http://www.london-se1.co.uk/news/view/8181 |date=10 September 2015 }} Friday 3 April 2015, Bankside Press</ref> In 1987, Corbyn was arrested for the defacing of an [[SDP–Liberal Alliance]] poster, but cautioned and released without charge.<ref>{{cite news|title=In Brief – A Labour candidate's brother was arrested|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2507&dat=19870611&id=Y0VAAAAAIBAJ&pg=5031,2867460|work=The Glasgow Herald|date=11 June 1987|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718210400/https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2507&dat=19870611&id=Y0VAAAAAIBAJ&pg=5031%2C2867460|url-status=live}}</ref>  For seven years he was an unpaid campaigns organiser in [[Southwark and Bermondsey (UK Parliament constituency)|Southwark and Bermondsey]], being thanked by [[Tony Blair]] in 1998 at Downing Street.<ref>Paul Vallely [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/he-visited-in-glory-days-of-97-but-has-blair-kept-his-vow-to-aylesbury-estate-6148476.html He visited in glory days of '97, but has Blair kept his vow to Aylesbury Estate?] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150702045026/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/he-visited-in-glory-days-of-97-but-has-blair-kept-his-vow-to-aylesbury-estate-6148476.html |date=2 July 2015 }} ''The Independent'', Tuesday 12 April 2005</ref> Corbyn left the Labour Party in 2002 in the run up to the [[2003 invasion of Iraq|invasion of Iraq]],<ref name="Wheeler">{{cite news|last1=Wheeler|first1=Caroline|last2=Leake|first2=Jonathan|url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/jeremy-corbyns-brother-piers-rejected-by-labour-t9m5bwktn|title=Jeremy Corbyn's brother Piers rejected by Labour|work=The Sunday Times|date=24 September 2017|access-date=24 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170924140304/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/edition/news/jeremy-corbyns-brother-piers-rejected-by-labour-t9m5bwktn|archive-date=24 September 2017|url-status=live}}{{subscription required}}</ref> and stood as an independent candidate in [[2002 Southwark London Borough Council election|2002]] and in a [[2014 Southwark London Borough Council election|2015 council by-election]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Chaucer by-election nears |url=https://www.southwarknews.co.uk/news/candidates-prepare-for-chaucer-ward-by-election/ |work=Southwark News |date=30 April 2015}}</ref> According to ''[[The Sunday Times]]'' in September 2017, his attempt to rejoin the Southwark [[Constituency Labour Party]] in January 2017 was blocked.<ref name="Wheeler"/>

His brother, [[Jeremy Corbyn]], was elected MP for [[Islington North (UK Parliament constituency)|Islington North]] in 1983, was re-elected in every following election {{As of|2025|lc=y}}, and served as Leader of the Labour Party and hence [[Leader of the Opposition (United Kingdom)|Leader of the Opposition]] from 2015 to 2020. In August 2015, Corbyn supported his brother's [[2015 Jeremy Corbyn Labour Party leadership campaign|campaign]] in the [[2015 Labour Party (UK) leadership election|Labour Party leadership election]], on the basis that he stood for proper debate and accountability, including on climate.<ref>[http://www.southwarknews.co.uk/news/piers-corbyn-denies-claims-in-media-that-he-opposes-brother-jeremys-labour-leadership-bid/ Piers Corbyn denies claims that he opposes brother Jeremy's Labour leadership bid] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151024121249/http://www.southwarknews.co.uk/news/piers-corbyn-denies-claims-in-media-that-he-opposes-brother-jeremys-labour-leadership-bid/ |date=24 October 2015 }} Southwark News, 20 August 2015</ref><ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2016/jan/24/piers-corbyn-other-rebel-in-the-family-jeremy-corbyn-climate-change Piers Corbyn: the other rebel in the family"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191222131144/https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2016/jan/24/piers-corbyn-other-rebel-in-the-family-jeremy-corbyn-climate-change |date=22 December 2019 }}, ''The Guardian''. Retrieved on 5 March 2018.</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Usborne|first1=Simon|date=14 August 2015|title=Is there trouble ahead for Jeremy Corbyn? Enter sibling Piers, the wacky weatherman...|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/is-there-trouble-ahead-for-jeremy-corbyn-enter-sibling-piers-the-wacky-weatherman-10454680.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213160717/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/is-there-trouble-ahead-for-jeremy-corbyn-enter-sibling-piers-the-wacky-weatherman-10454680.html|archive-date=13 December 2019|access-date=13 November 2018|work=The Independent}}</ref> On Twitter, he urged people to register to vote and back Jeremy Corbyn to lead the Labour Party.<ref name="twitter">{{cite web|last=Corbyn|first=Piers|url=https://twitter.com/Piers_Corbyn/status/630995541204336640|title=ONLY poll that counts open14Aug. Back #JeremyCorbyn 2lead Labour! Register 2vote by Midday12Aug #Corbyn4Labour #Piers|publisher=Twitter|date=11 August 2015|access-date=15 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191007033748/https://twitter.com/Piers_Corbyn/status/630995541204336640|archive-date=7 October 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

In March 2016, Corbyn was among a group of protesters at a Lambeth council meeting who reportedly "screamed abuse in the faces" of party councillors. Corbyn later told the BBC that he personally sought to make his points by talking to people, rather than shouting.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jeremy Corbyn's brother 'part of Lambeth council meeting disruption'|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-35896821|work=BBC News|last=Mason|first=Chris|date=24 March 2016|access-date=2 May 2021|archive-date=2 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210502113955/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-35896821|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== WeatherAction ===
Following some years of weather prediction as an occupation, he formed WeatherAction, a business, in 1995.<ref name=Wired/> WeatherAction is the business through which Corbyn sells his predictions. He has in the past bet on these predictions. His betting attracted much interest in 1990, when his predictions of severe weather were met by a year of the "worst extremes".<ref>{{cite news|title=Weather: The man who makes money out of sun-spots|work=[[The Independent]]|date=24 October 1997}}</ref>

WeatherAction was formerly listed company on the [[Alternative Investment Market]] (AIM) as 'Weather Action Holdings plc' in 1997,<ref>{{cite news|title=Haven't the foggiest? Read on |work=[[The Independent]]|date=22 November 1998|quote=Said to be listed "13 months" prior to publication, ie 1997}}</ref> and was transferred back to private ownership in 1999, primarily because of sustaining increasing losses and the impact of annual £70,000 costs related to listed status on annual revenues of £250,000.<ref name="guardian_1999">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/1999/nov/24/14|work=The Guardian|location=London|title=Weather goes private again|first=Dan|last=Atkinson|date=24 November 1999|access-date=22 May 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140507195112/http://www.theguardian.com/business/1999/nov/24/14|archive-date=7 May 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> Corbyn reacquired the weather prediction business; the listed shell was taken over by investors and changed its name to ''<nowiki>'InternetAction.com'</nowiki>'', with the intent of researching potential net-based takeover targets.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/1999/dec/21/efinance.internet2|work=The Guardian|location=London|title=Netvest shows 500% return|first=Terry|last=MacAlister|date=21 December 1999|access-date=22 May 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140507195740/http://www.theguardian.com/business/1999/dec/21/efinance.internet2|archive-date=7 May 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

WeatherAction left the Alternative Investment Market in 1999 after reported losses of £480,000 incurred during its time as a public company; its share price dropped from 79p a share to 24p.<ref name="guardian_1999" />

==== Prediction methods ====
Corbyn's technique is stated to combine "statistical analysis of over a century of historical weather patterns with clues derived from solar observations."<ref name=Wired/> He considers past weather patterns and solar observations and sun-earth magnetic connectivity. However, [[meteorology|meteorological]] studies show that such influences cause minimal impact on the Earth's [[atmosphere]].<ref name="BBC sun">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/6290228.stm|title='No Sun link' to climate change|access-date=7 January 2008|date=10 June 2007|work=[[BBC News]]|first=Richard|last=Black |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070913042521/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk/6290228.stm |archive-date=13 September 2007 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Scientific review ====
The only study involving Corbyn's work published in a peer-reviewed journal was in the ''[[Journal of Atmospheric and Solar-Terrestrial Physics]]'' (2001). Its investigation was limited to Corbyn's "likely damaging gale periods" predictions for the island of Great Britain for the period October 1995 – September 1997. Corbyn's enlisted work (carried out for a consortium of insurance companies) was only for the most likely periods of the strongest winds and specifically not a full forecast to include lesser winds:<ref>''The Journal of Atmospheric and Solar-Terrestrial Physics'', vol. 63, issue 1, January 2001, pp. 29–34:
[http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1364682600001553] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120616201500/http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1364682600001553|date=16 June 2012}}  URL accessed 8 September 2015. DOI 10.1016/S1364-6826(00)00155-3</ref>
{{blockquote|Forecasts prepared by WeatherAction would repay further attention. The results provide little evidence to dismiss the observed success rates as being attributable to mere chance or good fortune. Indeed the balance of evidence indicates that the system performs better than chance although it is recognized that the margin of success differs greatly between the seasons and is lowest in winter when gales are most frequent.<br />
This analysis has been wholly empirical in nature, seeking only to establish the success levels of the gale forecasts. Other aspects of the forecasts have not been considered in this evaluation. Inevitably however these results draw into the debate questions surrounding the methodology by which the forecasts are prepared. This is not, however, the arena in which such issues should be taken up.}}

In a 1999 edition of ''[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]'' magazine, researchers [[Ian Jolliffe]] and [[Nils Jolliffe]] stated of Corbyn's predictions that:<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Brekke |first=Dan |title=How Good Is He, Anyway? |date=1 February 1999 |magazine=Wired |issue=7.02 |url=https://www.wired.com/1999/02/howgood/}}</ref> "It is unusual for most of the detail to be completely correct, but equally it is rare for nearly everything to be wrong… Some forecasts are clearly very good, and a few are very poor, but the majority fall in the grey area in between, where an optimistic assessor would find merit, but a critical assessor would find fault."

In a 2012 article in ''Wired'' titled "The Fraudulent Business of Earthquake and Eruption Prediction",<ref>{{cite magazine|title=The fraudulent business of earthquake and eruption prediction|magazine=Wired|url=https://www.wired.com/2012/04/the-fraudulent-business-of-earthquake-and-eruption-prediction/|access-date=11 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130124132203/http://www.wired.com/wiredscience/2012/04/the-fraudulent-business-of-earthquake-and-eruption-prediction/|archive-date=24 January 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Erik Klemetti]], an assistant professor of Geosciences at Ohio's [[Denison University]] accused Corbyn of "[[Cherry picking (fallacy)|cherry-picking]]" and said people who claimed to be able to [[Earthquake prediction|forecast earthquakes]] were "faith healers of the geologic community and should be seen as such."

==== Media coverage ====
Critics have pointed to inaccurate predictions, such as a white Easter in 1989,<ref>[https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg12216605.200-feedback-.html Feedback – 15 April 1989 – New Scientist] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022014614/http://www.newscientist.com/article/mg12216605.200-feedback-.html |date=22 October 2012 }} (Subscription only)</ref> and "raging weather" in September 1997.<ref name="haven't the foggiest">{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/havent-the-foggiest-read-on-1186676.html |title=Haven't the foggiest? |work=The Independent |access-date=20 November 2010 |location=London |first=Matthew |last=Rowan |date=22 November 1998 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121110060136/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/havent-the-foggiest-read-on-1186676.html |archive-date=10 November 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref> WeatherAction predictions were contested by the [[Met Office]] in 2008.<ref>"[https://www.theguardian.com/weather/Story/0,,2233967,00.html Prediction of −17 °C freeze cuts no ice with Met Office] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718210401/https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2008/jan/02/weather.world |date=18 July 2021 }}" Helen Pidd, ''The Guardian'', January 2008</ref>

While he was [[Mayoralty of Boris Johnson|Mayor of London]], [[Boris Johnson]] repeatedly suggested that Corbyn might be correct in his denial of anthropogenic climate change.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newstatesman.com/politics/2013/01/boris-johnsons-climate-change-scepticism-embarrassment-londons-scientists| title= Boris Johnson's climate change "scepticism" is an embarrassment to London's scientists| website= [[New Statesman]]| first= Bob| last= Ward| author-link= Bob Ward (communications director)| date= 23 January 2013| access-date= 16 May 2020| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200105110609/https://www.newstatesman.com/politics/2013/01/boris-johnsons-climate-change-scepticism-embarrassment-londons-scientists| archive-date= 5 January 2020| url-status= live}}</ref>[[File:Piers Corbyn 2011-10-19 21 El Ser Creativo.png|thumb|right|Corbyn speaking at a 2011 ''El Ser Creativo'' event]]

=== Let London Live ===
In January 2021, it was announced that Corbyn would stand for his own party, Let London Live, in the [[2021 London mayoral election]] and [[2021 London Assembly election]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Corbyn|first=Piers|date=1 January 2021|title=I Announce Running For Mayor Of London – special VID 31st embargoed to midnight.|url=https://twitter.com/Piers_Corbyn/status/1344840096101638145?s=20|access-date=2 January 2021|website=Twitter|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718210410/https://twitter.com/account/suspended|url-status=live}}</ref> On 19 April, Corbyn told the BBC that if he were to be elected then he would "end lockdown on day one as mayor".<ref>{{cite web|title=Piers Corbyn: 'I will end lockdown on day one as mayor'|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/uk-england-london-56773522|website=BBC|date=19 April 2021|access-date=30 April 2021|archive-date=30 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210430105336/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/uk-england-london-56773522|url-status=live}}</ref> He finished 11th with 20,604 votes (0.8%) in the mayoral election, while his party finished 12th on the London-wide list with 15,755 votes.<ref>{{cite web|date=9 May 2021|title=Results 2021|url=https://www.londonelects.org.uk/im-voter/election-results/results-2021|access-date=9 May 2021|website=London Elects|language=en-GB|archive-date=8 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210508230654/https://www.londonelects.org.uk/im-voter/election-results/results-2021|url-status=live}}</ref> He stood for Let London Live in the [[2022 Southwark London Borough Council election]].

He stood as a candidate in the [[2023 Uxbridge and South Ruislip by-election]] for Let London Live;<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 June 2023 |title=Uxbridge by-election full candidate list revealed |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-london-66000978 |access-date=24 June 2023 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> Corbyn finished 11th of 17 candidates, receiving 101 votes (0.3%).<ref>{{cite web |title=Uxbridge and South Ruislip by-election 2023 results |url=https://www.hillingdon.gov.uk/by-election-results |website=Hillingdon Council |access-date=21 July 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

Let London Live was deregistered as a political party in November 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=Let London Live Party registration|url= https://search.electoralcommission.org.uk/English/Registrations/PP12768|website=The Electoral Commission|access-date=19 February 2024|language=en}}</ref>

As an independent he stood in [[Bermondsey and Old Southwark (UK Parliament constituency)|Bermondsey and Old Southwark]] constituency in the [[2024 United Kingdom general election|2024 general election]]; he received 403 votes (1.1%).

In 2025 it was announced he had joined [[Your Party (UK)|Your Party]] which had been co-founded by his brother earlier that year.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Myerson |first1=Sam |title=Piers Corbyn has no place in the left |url=https://www.workersliberty.org/story/2026-02-09/piers-corbyn-has-no-place-left?language_content_entity=en |access-date=3 March 2026 |date=9 February 2026}}</ref> In 2026 Piers Corbyn stood for the Central Executive Committee of Your Party in the London region. He was not elected coming 10th out of 13 candidates.<ref>{{cite web |title=Candidates for CEC Elections |url=https://www.yourparty.uk/cec-candidates/ |website=Your Party |access-date=3 March 2026}}</ref>

== Promotion of conspiracy theories ==
In 2020, Corbyn was reported by [[Hope not Hate]] and the [[Community Security Trust]] to have attended a meeting organised by [[Keep Talking (group)|Keep Talking]], a conspiracy theory discussion group based in the United Kingdom which has invited on occasion guest speakers involved in [[Holocaust denial]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Townsend |first1=Mark |title=UK left activists attended events with far right antisemites |url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2020/feb/22/uk-left-activists-at-far-right-events-antisemites-holocaust-deniers |access-date=24 April 2020 |work=[[The Observer]] |date=22 February 2020 |quote=Also present in the audience was Ian Fantom, co-founder of Keep Talking and a 9/11 "truther", who has appeared alongside Piers Corbyn, older brother of the Labour leader, at a Keep Talking event. |archive-date=13 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200513122506/https://www.theguardian.com/news/2020/feb/22/uk-left-activists-at-far-right-events-antisemites-holocaust-deniers |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Rich |first1=Dave |author1-link=Dave Rich |last2=Muhall |first2=Joe |title=Inside Keep Talking |url=https://cst.org.uk/data/file/6/c/keep-talking-2020-02.1582535588.pdf |publisher=Hope not Hate and Community Security Trust |pages=1–28 |archive-date=10 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200310110628/https://cst.org.uk/data/file/6/c/keep-talking-2020-02.1582535588.pdf |url-status=live|quote=Piers Corbyn, older brother of Jeremy, has attended several meetings and addressed at least one event.}}</ref>

===Climate change denial===
{{See also|Climate change denial}}
Corbyn rejects the [[scientific consensus on climate change]]. He [[Climate change denial|denies]] that humans play a role in [[climate change]], and spreads false and discredited narratives about the issue. He has said that the [[Media coverage of climate change|media]], [[Met Office]] and "corrupt scientists" are brainwashing the public as part of a Qatar-run conspiracy to keep oil prices high.<ref name="climate1">{{cite web|date=13 August 2015|title=Is there trouble ahead for Jeremy Corbyn? Enter sibling Piers, the wacky weatherman...|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/is-there-trouble-ahead-for-jeremy-corbyn-enter-sibling-piers-the-wacky-weatherman-10454680.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213160717/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/is-there-trouble-ahead-for-jeremy-corbyn-enter-sibling-piers-the-wacky-weatherman-10454680.html|archive-date=13 December 2019|access-date=8 September 2017|newspaper=The Independent}}</ref>

Corbyn has stated his belief that the [[Anthropogenic greenhouse gases|anthropogenic]] contribution to global warming is minimal, with any increase in temperature due to increased solar activity.<ref>{{cite web|last=Adams|first=Tim|date=24 January 2016|title=Piers Corbyn: the other rebel in the family|url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2016/jan/24/piers-corbyn-other-rebel-in-the-family-jeremy-corbyn-climate-change|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191222131144/https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2016/jan/24/piers-corbyn-other-rebel-in-the-family-jeremy-corbyn-climate-change|archive-date=22 December 2019|access-date=5 October 2019|work=[[The Observer]]}}</ref> In 2009 he attended the [[International Conference on Climate Change]] organised by [[the Heartland Institute]].<ref>[https://www.independent.co.uk/environment/climate-change/thinktanks-take-oil-money-and-use-it-to-fund-climate-deniers-1891747.html Think-tanks take oil money and use it to fund climate deniers] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923004521/http://www.independent.co.uk/environment/climate-change/thinktanks-take-oil-money-and-use-it-to-fund-climate-deniers-1891747.html|date=23 September 2015}} ''The Independent'', 7 February 2010</ref>

Corbyn featured in a Channel 4 documentary ''[[The Great Global Warming Swindle]]'' in 2007; a scientifically reviewed complaint to [[Ofcom]] noted that he was introduced as 'Dr Piers Corbyn, Climate Forecaster' despite not having a doctorate nor any qualification specifically in [[climate science]] or [[environmental science]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Full Ofcom Complaint, Table of Contents, page i|url=http://www.ofcomswindlecomplaint.net/FullComplaint/TOCp1.htm|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304033331/http://www.ofcomswindlecomplaint.net/FullComplaint/TOCp1.htm|archive-date=4 March 2016|access-date=11 September 2015}}</ref> In a 2016 interview Corbyn suggested that [[Margaret Thatcher]] endorsed the idea of man-made climate change as a strategy for phasing out the British coal industry and defeating the miners union in the [[UK miners' strike (1984–85)|1984–85 miners' strike]].<ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2016/jan/24/piers-corbyn-other-rebel-in-the-family-jeremy-corbyn-climate-change Piers Corbyn: the other rebel in the family] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191222131144/https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2016/jan/24/piers-corbyn-other-rebel-in-the-family-jeremy-corbyn-climate-change|date=22 December 2019}} ''The Observer'', Tim Adams, 24 January 2016</ref>  However, there is no evidence that Thatcher used environmental arguments about climate change at the time; her support for climate change policies did not start until later in the 1980s.<ref>{{cite web |last1=The Independent |title=What did Margaret Thatcher have to say about climate change? |website=[[Independent.co.uk]] |date=8 August 2021 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/margaret-thatcher-coal-mines-boris-johnson-b1899098.html |access-date=28 September 2023}}</ref>

In 2015, [[BBC Radio 4]] apologised for an "unfortunate lapse" in a documentary presented by ''[[Daily Mail]]'' journalist [[Quentin Letts]], which featured Corbyn in a critique of the Met Office's views on climate change while failing to mention the [[scientific consensus]].<ref>[https://www.independent.co.uk/news/media/tv-radio/bbc-apologises-for-documentary-that-criticised-met-office-over-climate-change-a6684896.html What's The Point of… the Met Office?] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170914015730/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/media/tv-radio/bbc-apologises-for-documentary-that-criticised-met-office-over-climate-change-a6684896.html|date=14 September 2017}} Ian Burrell, October 2015, ''The Independent''</ref>

In March 2016, Corbyn participated in a BBC climate change debate which resulted in several people complaining to the BBC for giving him airtime.<ref>{{cite web|title=Viewers criticise BBC for 'misleading' Piers Corbyn appearance|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/bbc/12199709/Viewers-criticise-BBC-for-misleading-Piers-Corbyn-appearance.html|work=The Telegraph|last=Ward|first=Victoria|date=20 March 2016|access-date=2 May 2021|archive-date=2 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210502122757/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/bbc/12199709/Viewers-criticise-BBC-for-misleading-Piers-Corbyn-appearance.html|url-status=live}}{{subscription required}}</ref>

He was interviewed by Dutch filmmaker [[Marijn Poels]] for his 2017 documentary feature film about climate, energy and agriculture, called ''[[The Uncertainty Has Settled]]''.<ref>{{cite web | last=Verheggen | first=Bart | title=A critical look at "The uncertainty has settled" documentary by Marijn Poels | website=My view on climate change | date=17 July 2017 | url=https://ourchangingclimate.wordpress.com/2017/07/17/a-critical-look-at-the-uncertainty-has-settled-documentary-by-marijn-poels/ | access-date=21 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | first=Andrew |last=Reid | title="The Uncertainty Has Settled", a feature film shot using Magic Lantern raw video – Filmmaking Gear and Camera Reviews | website=EOSHD.com – Filmmaking Gear and Camera Reviews | date=10 October 2017 | url=https://www.eoshd.com/news/uncertainty-settled-feature-film-shot-using-magic-lantern-raw-video/ | access-date=21 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Jakobs | first=Jan | title=The Uncertainty Has Settled | website=Marijn Poels | date=3 March 2017 | url=https://www.marijnpoels.com/single-post/2017/03/03/the-uncertainty-has-settled-a-deadly-earnest-search | access-date=21 September 2022 | others=Original review – ''De Doorbraak'' / Written by: Jan Jacobs, politics and science journalist }}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

In April 2019, Corbyn tweeted about the Swedish environmental activist [[Greta Thunberg]] with an image of her next to a Nazi [[swastika]], describing her as an "ignorant, brainwashed child".<ref>{{cite news|title=Who is Jeremy Corbyn's brother Piers? Mask protests, climate denial and support for a no-deal Brexit|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/men/thinking-man/covid-protests-climate-denial-family-nightmare-jeremy-corbyns/|work=The Telegraph|last=Shute|first=Joe|date=31 August 2020|access-date=6 September 2020|archive-date=6 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200906222346/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/men/thinking-man/covid-protests-climate-denial-family-nightmare-jeremy-corbyns/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In April 2023 Corbyn was removed from an Extinction Rebellion church service in London after gatecrashing the event and telling environmental activists that man-made climate change "does not exist" and that they were "working for the Devil". The crowd, which had gathered for a service titled "No Faith in Fossil Fuels", began to sing the hymn "Amazing Grace" as he was escorted away.<ref>{{cite web |last1=The Independent |title=Piers Corbyn gatecrashes Extinction Rebellion church service to tell eco-activists they're 'working for the Devil' |website=[[Independent.co.uk]] |date=21 April 2023 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/piers-corbyn-extinction-rebellion-london-b2324466.html |access-date=30 September 2023}}</ref>

=== COVID-19 denial ===
{{See also|Misinformation related to the COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19 vaccine misinformation and hesitancy|COVID-19 protests in the United Kingdom}}{{Very long|date=December 2021|nosplit=y|section}}
Corbyn has stated his belief that [[COVID-19]] and the associated [[COVID-19 pandemic|ongoing pandemic]] is a "hoax".<ref name="Times20200911">{{cite news|last1=Kennedy|first1=Dominic|last2=Ellis|first2=Rosa|title=ANTIVAX Piers Corbyn blamed for split among coronavirus deniers|url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/healthcare/article/piers-corbyn-blamed-for-split-among-coronavirus-deniers-hq3lm333c|work=The Times|date=11 September 2020|access-date=12 September 2020|archive-date=11 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200911171359/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/piers-corbyn-blamed-for-split-among-coronavirus-deniers-hq3lm333c|url-status=live}}{{subscription required}}</ref> On Twitter on 16 March 2020, he tweeted from an account that was later suspended an unfounded conspiracy theory that [[Bill Gates]], [[George Soros]] and others had created the pandemic, that this was to mass vaccinate the world's population, and that vaccines are dangerous.<ref>{{Cite web |title=PECR – cyber attacks soar during coronavirus |last=Irwin |first=Luke |work=IT Governance UK |date=17 March 2020 |url= https://www.itgovernance.co.uk/blog/hackers-exploit-coronavirus-fears-as-cyber-attacks-soar}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=York|first=Chris|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/piers-corbyn_uk_5eedb613c5b6996a0b16abd1|title=Jeremy Corbyn's Brother, Piers, Charged With Breaching Coronavirus Regulations At 5G Protest|work=HuffPost|date=14 September 2020|orig-year=20 June 2020|access-date=15 December 2020|archive-date=20 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620071751/https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/piers-corbyn_uk_5eedb613c5b6996a0b16abd1|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=5 dangerous coronavirus claims made by Piers Corbyn at Glastonbury anti-lockdown protest debunked|url=https://www.somersetlive.co.uk/news/somerset-news/coronavirus-myths-piers-corbyn-lockdown-4098881|work=Somerset News|last=Trim|first=Liam|date=3 May 2020|access-date=28 September 2020|archive-date=28 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201028194523/https://www.somersetlive.co.uk/news/somerset-news/coronavirus-myths-piers-corbyn-lockdown-4098881|url-status=live}}</ref> He called the pandemic a "psychological operation to close down the economy in the interests of mega-corporations" on [[Good Morning Britain (2014 TV programme)|''Good Morning Britain'']]; [[Hilary Jones (doctor)|Dr. Hilary Jones]] described his views as spurious and "extremely dangerous" and hosts [[Piers Morgan]] and [[Susanna Reid]] challenged him during the programme.<ref name=itv>{{Cite news |url=https://www.itv.com/goodmorningbritain/articles/piers-corbyn-covid-anti-lockdown-protest-dr-hilary |title=Anti-lockdown protestor Piers Corbyn challenged by Dr Hilary over COVID-19 'hoax' claims|work=ITV News|date=1 September 2020 |access-date=2 September 2020 |archive-date=2 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200902015815/https://www.itv.com/goodmorningbritain/articles/piers-corbyn-covid-anti-lockdown-protest-dr-hilary |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== 2020 ====
On 16 May 2020, Corbyn was one of 19 people arrested for refusing to leave and failing to provide details whilst protesting against the UK's [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 lockdown]] in [[Hyde Park, London|Hyde Park]], London. On this occasion, he advocated [[Misinformation related to the COVID-19 pandemic|coronavirus-related 5G conspiracy theories]] and [[Anti-vaccine activism|anti-vaccination claims]] before being arrested.<ref name="Guardian-16-May-2020">{{cite news|title=Piers Corbyn among 19 held in coronavirus lockdown protests|work=The Guardian|last=Parveen|first=Nazia|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/may/16/piers-corbyn-among-those-held-in-coronavirus-lockdown-protests|date=16 May 2020|access-date=16 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620232608/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/may/16/piers-corbyn-among-those-held-in-coronavirus-lockdown-protests|archive-date=20 June 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Dearden|first=Lizzie|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/coronavirus-protests-hyde-park-london-jeremy-corbyn-piers-brother-lockdown-a9518341.html |title=Coronavirus protests: Jeremy Corbyn's brother among protesters arrested at Hyde Park 'mass gathering'|work=The Independent|date=16 May 2020|access-date=18 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200602081950/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/coronavirus-protests-hyde-park-london-jeremy-corbyn-piers-brother-lockdown-a9518341.html |archive-date=2 June 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Bird|first=Steve|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/05/16/anger-mounts-visitors-flock-beauty-spots-national-parks/|title='Wish you weren't here': Anger mounts as visitors flock to beauty spots and national parks|work=The Telegraph|date=16 May 2020|access-date=15 December 2020|archive-date=27 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201127161732/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/05/16/anger-mounts-visitors-flock-beauty-spots-national-parks/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 30 May, Corbyn attended another protest at Hyde Park, and was again charged with, as described in ''[[The Independent]]'', "contravening coronavirus rules".<ref name=indy/>

On 29 August, Corbyn was arrested by the [[Metropolitan Police]] near [[Trafalgar Square]] and warned he would be issued with a [[fixed penalty notice]] (FPN) for £10,000, on suspicion of breaking new [[The Health Protection (Coronavirus, Restrictions) (No. 2) (England) Regulations 2020|Health Protection Regulations (2020)]] for the offence of holding a gathering of more than 30 people in an outdoor place. He appeared alongside conspiracy theorist [[David Icke]] and singer [[Chico Slimani]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=York |first1=Chris|title=Jeremy Corbyn's Brother Piers Fined £10,000 Over Trafalgar Square Anti-Mask Protest |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/piers-corbyn-fined-arrested_uk_5f4bf36cc5b6cf66b2b978db |access-date=30 August 2020 |work=HuffPost|date=30 August 2020 |archive-date=1 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101152217/https://consent.yahoo.com/v2/collectConsent?sessionId=2_cc-session_c681173e-4ecc-4c46-af1d-d2519b48a755 |url-status=live }}</ref> Corbyn was fined £10,000 for organising an anti-lockdown rally in Trafalgar Square, London.<ref>{{cite news|last=Gayle|first=Damien|title=Piers Corbyn fined £10,000 for organising anti-lockdown rally|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/30/piers-corbyn-fined-10000-for-organising-anti-lockdown-rally|work=The Guardian|date=30 August 2020|access-date=2 September 2020|archive-date=21 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200921005704/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/30/piers-corbyn-fined-10000-for-organising-anti-lockdown-rally|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 5 September, Corbyn attended and helped to organise an anti-lockdown rally organised by StandUpX Mission in [[Sheffield]]. During the rally he argued: that the lockdown was taking place so the British government can "end your rights and freedom, to control you"; that the shift to mass vaccination was dangerous; and that the British government have a hidden agenda. At the end of the rally, Corbyn was arrested<ref name=thestar>{{cite news|title='We are now a movement' Piers Corbyn tells hundreds at Sheffield 'anti-mask' protest|url=https://www.thestar.co.uk/news/people/we-are-now-movement-piers-corbyn-tells-hundreds-sheffield-anti-mask-protest-2962878|work=The Star|date=6 September 2020|access-date=7 September 2020|archive-date=1 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101152155/https://www.thestar.co.uk/news/people/we-are-now-movement-piers-corbyn-tells-hundreds-sheffield-anti-mask-protest-2962878|url-status=live}}</ref> and charged with three offences under the Health Protection (Coronavirus) Regulations 2020.<ref name=indy>{{cite news|title=Piers Corbyn charged with breaking coronavirus laws|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/piers-corbyn-coronavirus-protest-sheffield-charge-police-b406287.html?amp|work=The Independent|agency=Press Association|first1=Catherine|last1=Wylie|date=8 September 2020|access-date=8 September 2020|archive-date=1 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101152154/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/piers-corbyn-coronavirus-protest-sheffield-charge-police-b406287.html?amp|url-status=live}}</ref> The charges were later dropped.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-south-yorkshire-54780190|title=Coronavirus: Piers Corbyn Sheffield charges dropped|work=BBC News|date=2 November 2020|access-date=15 December 2020|archive-date=26 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201126143609/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-south-yorkshire-54780190|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 6 September, Corbyn invited [[Sadiq Khan]] to permit a rally in [[Trafalgar Square]] London at noon on 26 September, and he invited MPs of any party to speak from the podium at the London rally.<ref name="ytpc">{{cite web |last1=Corbyn |first1=Piers |title="OUR MOVEMENT, WE CAN WIN" Says Piers Corbyn |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2bjCkG6n0RI |publisher=YouTube |date=6 September 2020 |access-date=10 September 2020 |archive-date=6 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200906192210/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2bjCkG6n0RI&gl=US&hl=en |url-status=live }}</ref> On 18 September, Corbyn spoke at a rally in Cornwall against the use of [[cloth face mask|face masks]] to protect against COVID-19, and described all politicians as liars.<ref>{{cite news|last=Trewhela|first=Lee|title=Piers Corbyn calls brother Jeremy a liar at controversial Cornwall anti-mask rally|url=https://www.cornwalllive.com/news/cornwall-news/piers-corbyn-calls-brother-jeremy-4529625|work=CornwallLive|date=18 September 2020|access-date=20 September 2020|archive-date=24 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200924054502/https://www.cornwalllive.com/news/cornwall-news/piers-corbyn-calls-brother-jeremy-4529625|url-status=live}}</ref> On 24 September, Corbyn was one of the main speakers at an anti-mask rally in Norwich.<ref>{{cite news|title=Piers Corbyn leads coronavirus sceptics protest in Norwich|url=https://www.eveningnews24.co.uk/news/protesters-bring-coronavirus-scepticism-demonstration-to-norwich-1-6853860|work=Norwich Evening News|date=24 September 2020|access-date=27 September 2020|archive-date=26 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200926053121/https://www.eveningnews24.co.uk/news/protesters-bring-coronavirus-scepticism-demonstration-to-norwich-1-6853860|url-status=live}}</ref> On 26 September, Corbyn attended a rally in Leeds and repeated the claims he had made in Cornwall.<ref>{{cite news|last=Drury|first=Colin|title=This is genocide': Inside the bizarre rise of coronavirus conspiracy theories|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/coronavirus-conspiracy-theories-bill-gates-hoax-vaccine-5g-qanon-protest-piers-corbyn-b575326.html?amp|work=The Independent|date=26 September 2020|access-date=27 September 2020|archive-date=16 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201016042022/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/coronavirus-conspiracy-theories-bill-gates-hoax-vaccine-5g-qanon-protest-piers-corbyn-b575326.html?amp|url-status=live}}</ref> By mid-September, Corbyn had been blamed for a split among conspiracy theorists promoting misinformation about COVID-19, with [[Kate Shemirani]] and  [[Mark Steele (conspiracy theorist)|Mark Steele]] no longer sharing platforms with Corbyn and [[David Icke]].<ref name="Times20200911" />

On 3 October, Corbyn attended and spoke at an anti-lockdown protest at [[Old Market Square, Nottingham|Old Market Square]] in Nottingham.<ref>{{cite news|title=Opinion: Anti-lockdown protest in Nottingham fails to grasp complexity of the pandemic|url=https://www.nottinghampost.com/news/news-opinion/opinion-anti-lockdown-protest-nottingham-4574086.amp|work=Nottingham Post|date=4 October 2020|access-date=5 October 2020|archive-date=7 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201007100813/https://www.nottinghampost.com/news/news-opinion/opinion-anti-lockdown-protest-nottingham-4574086.amp|url-status=live}}</ref> On 9 October, Corbyn attended an anti-lockdown event in Oxford.<ref>{{cite news|title=Piers Corbyn speaks at coronavirus demonstration in Oxford|url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/18784744.piers-corbyn-speaks-coronavirus-demonstration-oxford/|work=Oxford Mail|first=Liam|last=Rice|date=10 October 2020|access-date=15 October 2020|archive-date=17 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017005702/https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/18784744.piers-corbyn-speaks-coronavirus-demonstration-oxford/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 11 October, Corbyn attended an anti-lockdown protest outside the [[Welsh Parliament]] in Cardiff. He expressed his opposition to masks and told protesters to "free your face".<ref>{{cite news|title=Covid rules breached at Cardiff anti-vaccination and anti-mask protest attended by Piers Corbyn|url=https://www.itv.com/news/wales/2020-10-12/covid-rules-breached-at-cardiff-anti-vaccination-and-anti-mask-protest-attended-by-piers-corbyn|work=ITV News|date=12 October 2020|access-date=15 October 2020|archive-date=14 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201014072904/https://www.itv.com/news/wales/2020-10-12/covid-rules-breached-at-cardiff-anti-vaccination-and-anti-mask-protest-attended-by-piers-corbyn|url-status=live}}</ref> On 14 October, Corbyn was the leader of an anti-lockdown protest in Sheffield. During his speech at the protest, he called for supporters to disobey public health restrictions. He described the British Parliament as a "brainwashing institution" that was full of "fake scientists" who are "paid liars".<ref>{{cite news|title=Piers Corbyn leads anti-lockdown protest in Sheffield and brands Covid-19 a 'hoax'|url=https://www.thestar.co.uk/news/politics/council/piers-corbyn-leads-anti-lockdown-protest-sheffield-and-brands-covid-19-hoax-3003622?amp|work=The Star|first=Molly|last=Williams|date=14 October 2020|access-date=15 October 2020|archive-date=19 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019205314/https://www.thestar.co.uk/news/politics/council/piers-corbyn-leads-anti-lockdown-protest-sheffield-and-brands-covid-19-hoax-3003622?amp|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 14 October, Corbyn attended an anti-lockdown protest in Bristol which was organised by the conspiracy theory group Stand UpX. He was one of fourteen people who were arrested for breaching new laws on assembly during the pandemic.<ref>{{cite news|last=Dearden|first=Lizzie|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/covid-lockdown-protest-piers-corbyn-bristol-arrest-b1723019.html|title=Lockdown protests: Jeremy Corbyn's brother arrested at conspiracy theorist demonstration in Bristol|work=The Independent|date=14 November 2020|access-date=15 December 2020|archive-date=19 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201219055825/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/covid-lockdown-protest-piers-corbyn-bristol-arrest-b1723019.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 16 October, Corbyn attended a demonstration in Soho, London, against the 10&nbsp;pm pub curfew. He said: "We're here to drink against the curfew. To oppose the lockdowns, to oppose job losses caused by lockdowns, to oppose all of it. The whole lot should be lifted now."<ref>{{cite news|title=Anti-lockdown marchers in London compare Covid-19 to man flu|url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/uk/anti-lockdown-marchers-in-london-compare-covid-19-to-man-flu-39635610.html|work=Belfast Telegraph|first=Tess de la|last=Mare|date=17 October 2020|access-date=18 October 2020|archive-date=1 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101152222/https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/uk/anti-lockdown-marchers-in-london-compare-covid-19-to-man-flu-39635610.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 17 October, Corbyn attended an anti-lockdown protest through Hyde Park and Oxford Street in London.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jeremy Corbyn's brother Piers joins lockdown rule-breaking revellers in central London|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/piers-corbyn-brother-lockdown-protest-soho-10pm-curfew-b1102512.html|work=The Independent|first=Liam|last=Coleman|date=17 October 2020|access-date=18 October 2020|archive-date=1 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101152157/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/piers-corbyn-brother-lockdown-protest-soho-10pm-curfew-b1102512.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Corbyn said to the crowd "[[Bill Gates]] wants vaccinations to control you and to control women's fertility to reduce world population".<ref>{{cite news|title=Anti-Lockdown Conspiracy Theorists March in London as New Tier 2 Rules Hit|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/standupx-anti-lockdown-protest-anti-mask-london/|work=VICE|first=Ruby|last=Lott-Lavigna|date=17 October 2020|access-date=18 October 2020|archive-date=19 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019072001/https://www.vice.com/en/article/93w9ke/standupx-anti-lockdown-protest-anti-mask-london|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 18 October, Corbyn attended an anti-lockdown protest in [[Clayton Square Shopping Centre|Clayton Square]], Liverpool City Centre. In a speech to protesters, he denied the existence of COVID-19, also suggested it was a [[bioweapon]], and said "it was used to unleash the most monstrous power-grab the world has ever seen".<ref>{{cite news|title=Conspiracy theorist Piers Corbyn tells crowd of unmasked protesters 'covid is a hoax'|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/conspiracy-theorist-piers-corbyn-tells-19125232|work=Liverpool Echo|first=Jonathan|last=Humphries|date=18 October 2020|access-date=18 October 2020|archive-date=19 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019060254/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/conspiracy-theorist-piers-corbyn-tells-19125232|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 24 October, Corbyn attended an anti-lockdown protest by Save Our Rights UK using the slogan "Stop The New Normal" in London.<ref>{{cite news|title=Police disperse fourth anti-lockdown march in London|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/oct/24/police-disperse-fourth-anti-lockdown-march-in-london|work=The Guardian|first=Damien|last=Gayle|date=24 October 2020|access-date=24 October 2020|archive-date=24 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024194105/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/oct/24/police-disperse-fourth-anti-lockdown-march-in-london|url-status=live}}</ref> The police determined that the protesters were not adhering to the coronavirus rules and decided to break up the protest. At least 18 people were arrested during the protest.<ref>{{cite news|title=Police make arrests at London anti-lockdown protest after risk assessment violated|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/anti-lockdown-protest-london-police-arrests-coronavirus-conspiracy-theorists-b1286036.html?amp|work=The Independent|last=Dearden|first=Lizzie|date=24 October 2020|access-date=24 October 2020|archive-date=28 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201028214725/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/anti-lockdown-protest-london-police-arrests-coronavirus-conspiracy-theorists-b1286036.html?amp|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Covid: At least 18 arrested at anti-lockdown protests in London|url=https://www.itv.com/news/2020-10-24/covid-at-least-18-arrested-at-anti-lockdown-protests-in-london|work=ITV News|date=24 October 2020|access-date=24 October 2020|archive-date=25 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201025011324/https://www.itv.com/news/2020-10-24/covid-at-least-18-arrested-at-anti-lockdown-protests-in-london|url-status=live}}</ref>

Corbyn was due to appear at [[Westminster Magistrates' Court]] on 17 November 2020 for breaching coronavirus rules on 16 and 30 May 2020. He was due to stand trial on 23 October 2020, but late disclosure of police logbooks delayed the proceedings.<ref name=guardian1>{{cite news|title=Police targeted Piers Corbyn at anti-lockdown protests, court told|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2020/oct/23/police-targeted-piers-corbyn-at-anti-lockdown-protests-court-told|work=The Guardian|agency=Press Association|date=23 October 2020|access-date=24 October 2020|archive-date=24 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024232831/https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2020/oct/23/police-targeted-piers-corbyn-at-anti-lockdown-protests-court-told|url-status=live}}</ref> Corbyn's barrister told the court that he was "specifically targeted" by the police.<ref name=guardian1 /> Corbyn spoke outside of the court before the hearing on 23 October 2020: "Whatever happens, if they impose a fine, I will not pay the fine. I'm not going to pay any fines for these anti-just, illegal laws".<ref>{{cite news|title=Piers Corbyn 'specifically targeted by police' at anti-lockdown protest court heard|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-54663466|work=BBC News|date=23 October 2020|access-date=24 October 2020|archive-date=24 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024125032/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-54663466|url-status=live}}</ref>

Corbyn initiated and conceptualised an anti-vaccination leaflet which was distributed in Barnet and other areas of North London in December 2020 and Southwark in January 2021 comparing the Covid vaccine campaign to the [[Holocaust]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Harpin|first=Lee|url=https://www.thejc.com/news/piers-corbyn-circulates-leaflets-in-north-london-comparing-vaccine-campaign-to-shoah-kq4idez4|title=Piers Corbyn circulates leaflets in north London comparing vaccine campaign to Shoah|work=The Jewish Chronicle|date=16 December 2020|access-date=2 February 2021|archive-date=5 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210205104301/https://www.thejc.com/news/uk/piers-corbyn-circulates-leaflets-in-north-london-comparing-vaccine-campaign-to-shoah-1.509743|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Gdn20210202">{{cite news|last=Quinn|first=Ben|url=https://www.theguardian.com/society/2021/feb/02/piers-corbyn-investigated-covid-leaflets-vaccination-to-auschwitz|title=Piers Corbyn investigated over Covid leaflets likening vaccination to Auschwitz|work=The Guardian|date=2 February 2021|access-date=2 February 2021|archive-date=2 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210202123457/https://www.theguardian.com/society/2021/feb/02/piers-corbyn-investigated-covid-leaflets-vaccination-to-auschwitz|url-status=live}}</ref> The leaflet had a drawing of the entrance to the [[Auschwitz concentration camp]] in which the [[Nazi]]s' slogan ''[[Arbeit macht frei]]'' ("Work sets you free") had been altered to read "Vaccines are safe path to freedom."<ref name="Gdn20210202" /> Corbyn denied the accusation of [[antisemitism]], saying, "I was married for 22 years to a Jewess and obviously her mother's forebears fled the Baltic states just before the war because of Hitler or the Nazis in general. I've worked with Jewish leading world scientists over the last 30 years. I've also employed Jewish people in my business Weather Action, one of whom was a superb worker".<ref>{{cite news|last=Fort|first=Mathilde|title=Piers Corbyn arrested but denies antisemitism, saying he was married to 'Jewess'|url=https://www.thejc.com/news/piers-corbyn-arrested-but-denies-antisemitism-saying-he-was-married-to-jewess-gi7bs5m3|work=The Jewish Chronicle|date=4 February 2021|access-date=30 April 2021|archive-date=2 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210502232730/https://www.thejc.com/news/uk/piers-corbyn-arrested-but-denies-antisemitism-saying-he-was-married-to-jewess-1.511503|url-status=live}}</ref>

==== 2021 ====
During a voluntary visit to a London police station, Corbyn was arrested on 3 February 2021 on suspicion of malicious communications and public nuisance in connection with the leaflet;<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-55933373|title=Piers Corbyn arrested over vaccine 'Auschwitz leaflet'|work=BBC News|date=4 February 2021|access-date=5 February 2021|archive-date=27 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210227031034/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-55933373|url-status=live}}</ref> he was released on bail until early March, along with a man aged 37.<ref>{{cite news|last=Quinn|first=Ben|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/feb/04/piers-corbyn-arrested-over-leaflets-comparing-covid-vaccine-programme-to-auschwitz|title=Piers Corbyn arrested over leaflets comparing vaccine programme to Auschwitz|work=The Guardian|date=4 February 2021|access-date=5 February 2021|archive-date=4 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210204220509/https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/feb/04/piers-corbyn-arrested-over-leaflets-comparing-covid-vaccine-programme-to-auschwitz|url-status=live}}</ref> Corbyn was arrested again at a protest in Fulham, West London on 27 February.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://au.news.yahoo.com/piers-corbyn-led-away-handcuffs-150000594.html|title=Piers Corbyn led away in handcuffs as he is arrested again at London anti-lockdown march|work=Yahoo! News|date=27 February 2021|access-date=28 February 2021|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718210402/https://au.news.yahoo.com/piers-corbyn-led-away-handcuffs-150000594.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In the meantime, he claimed to [[Sky News]] via email that, while he accepted the existence of COVID-19, he spuriously compared it to [[Influenza|flu]], contradicting his leaflet's claim that COVID does not exist, as well as denying that there was a pandemic.<ref name=Sky20210208>{{cite web|title=How COVID-conspiracists and anti-vaxxers are getting organised and making money|url=https://news.sky.com/story/how-covid-conspiracists-and-anti-vaxxers-are-getting-organised-and-making-money-12206707|work=Sky News|author=|date=8 February 2021|access-date=1 March 2021|archive-date=27 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210227193203/https://news.sky.com/story/how-covid-conspiracists-and-anti-vaxxers-are-getting-organised-and-making-money-12206707|url-status=live}}</ref> On 1 March the [[Metropolitan Police]] reported that Corbyn had been charged along with [[Kate Shemirani]] for a series of breaches of the UK Coronavirus regulations.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Five people charged with breaches of Coronavirus regulations|url=https://news.met.police.uk/news/five-people-charged-with-breaches-of-coronavirus-regulations-422234|url-status=live|work=Metropolitan Police|access-date=9 March 2021|archive-date=2 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210302020834/https://news.met.police.uk/news/five-people-charged-with-breaches-of-coronavirus-regulations-422234}}</ref>

In June, the police began investigating Corbyn after they became aware of a video that surfaced online of him removing public health signs informing people to maintain social distance and to wear a face mask on a London Underground train.<ref>{{cite news|title=Police investigating after Piers Corbyn removes social distancing signs from London Tube|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/piers-corbyn-british-transport-police-b1869054.html|work=The Independent|last=Goddard|first=Emily|date=19 June 2021|access-date=14 July 2021|archive-date=14 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210714075940/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/piers-corbyn-british-transport-police-b1869054.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 10 July, Corbyn and other anti-lockdown protesters staged a protest outside a vaccine centre bus in Brighton and Hove, which subsequently caused the NHS Brighton and Hove CCG to announce that they had to cancel some vaccine jabs because of "disruption during the anti-lockdown measures protest in the city". The protest was condemned by the Brighton and Hove council leader Phelim Mac Cafferty, who said, "It is incredibly disappointing to see the irresponsible actions of a few putting in danger the many."<ref>{{cite news|title=Brighton vaccine centre forced to cancel jabs after anti-lockdown protest involving Piers Corbyn|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/covid-vaccine-brighton-piers-corbyn-b1882147.html|work=The Independent|last=Glover|first=Ella|date=12 July 2021|access-date=14 July 2021|archive-date=14 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210714075941/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/covid-vaccine-brighton-piers-corbyn-b1882147.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 20 July, Corbyn attended and spoke at a protest outside the Labour Party's headquarters opposing the expulsion of Labour Party members who had been accused of antisemitism. He said that he was "100 per cent" behind "those being purged from the Labour Party".<ref name=headquarters>{{cite web|title= Piers Corbyn addresses protest outside Labour HQ against antisemitism expulsions|url=https://jewishnews.timesofisrael.com/piers-corbyn-addresses-protest-outside-labour-hq-against-expulsions/|website=Jewish News|last=Harpin|first=Lee|date=20 July 2021}}</ref> During his speech, Corbyn said that complying with the government's vaccine rollout was the same as the German people submitting to Nazi rule, stating, "You know what happened in Germany... they believed in Hitler. You know what happened, the rest is history".<ref name=headquarters /> Corbyn's attendance at the protest was not welcomed by everyone present at the protest, and some of the protesters distanced themselves from him due to his COVID-19 denial.<ref name=headquarters />

In July, YouTube pranksters [[Josh Pieters]] and [[Archie Manners]], posing as [[AstraZeneca]] investors, met Corbyn and offered him £10,000 under the condition that he would stop criticising the [[AstraZeneca vaccine]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Anti-vaxxer Piers Corbyn takes fake bribe from pranksters posing as Astrazeneca reps|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/tv/news/piers-corbyn-anti-vaxxer-prank-astrazeneca-v694f290c?amp|newspaper=The Independent|last=Brambilla|first=Chiara|date=1 August 2021}}</ref> In reality, Corbyn received ''[[Monopoly (game)|Monopoly]]'' board game money.<ref>{{cite news|last=Plummer|first=Kate|title=Piers Corbyn tricked into 'accepting' £10,000 on condition he stops criticising AstraZeneca vaccine |url=https://www.indy100.com/news/piers-corbyn-astrazeneca-covid-vaccine-b1894414|access-date=1 August 2021|work=[[The Independent]]|date=1 August 2021}}</ref> The pranksters told LBC when asked whether they feel sorry for Corbyn that they feel more sorry for "those he's conning".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lbc.co.uk/radio/presenters/tom-swarbrick/youtubers-josh-pieters-archie-manners-trick-piers-corbyn-astrazeneca-antivaxx/|title=Youtubers who tricked Piers Corbyn tell LBC they're more 'sorry for those he's conning'|work=LBC|last=Hickey|first=Seán|date=1 August 2021|access-date=23 August 2021}}</ref>

Corbyn was present at an anti-vaxxer demonstration on 9 August outside [[Television Centre, London|BBC's Television Centre]] in London (protesters falsely assumed it was still a major BBC facility) and outside the [[ITN]] building on [[Gray's Inn Road]] on 23 August 2021.<ref>{{cite news|last=Waterson|first=Jim|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/aug/09/confused-anti-vaccine-protesters-storm-bbc-hq-years-after-moved-out|title=Anti-vaccine protesters storm BBC HQ – years after it moved out|work=The Guardian|date=9 August 2021|access-date=23 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Parker|first1=Charlie|last2=Kanter|first2=Jake|url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/crime/article/antivaxers-storm-itn-studios-and-abuse-presenter-jon-snow-0hmj7hgxc|title=Antivaxers storm ITN studios and abuse presenter Jon Snow|work=The Times|date=23 August 2021|access-date=23 August 2021}} {{subscription required}}</ref>

In September 2021, Corbyn staged a protest outside the [[Old Bailey]] in London, on the day former [[Metropolitan Police]] officer Wayne Couzens was being [[Sentencing in England and Wales|sentenced]] for the [[murder of Sarah Everard]]. Corbyn said the fact that Couzens showed Everard his police [[warrant card]] and claimed to be arresting her for breaches of the UK's [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|lockdown regulations]] to kidnap her was evidence that coronavirus laws were "not about controlling a virus" but instead "about controlling the public". The protest was widely seen as inappropriate given the highly disturbing and emotive nature of the Everard murder, and a passerby approached Corbyn shouting "How dare you hijack Sarah's death for your own cause?".<ref>{{cite news|title=Sarah Everard: Fury as Piers Corbyn tries to use murder case to protest Covid lockdown laws outside court|url=https://inews.co.uk/news/uk/sarah-everard-case-protest-covid-lockdown-laws-court-piers-corbyn-wayne-couzens-1225497|work=i|last=Blackall|first=Molly|date=30 September 2021|access-date=4 October 2021}}</ref>

Corbyn attended another large demonstration against the UK government's proposed COVID restrictions on 18 December 2021 in [[Parliament Square]]. There, he featured in another music video, this time alongside rapper Remeece, in which they walk through crowds of protestors whilst repeatedly calling for viewers to refuse to take the [[COVID-19 vaccine]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=18 December 2021|title=Piers Corbyn has now made an anti-vaxx rap and it's truly dreadful|url=https://www.indy100.com/news/piers-corbyn-covid-rap-song-b1978713|access-date=18 December 2021|website=www.indy100.com|language=en}}</ref> In a later speech at the demonstration, Corbyn's comments on these proposals to enforce guidelines to combat the spread of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant|Omicron variant]] of the virus were met with widespread backlash. He had urged the crowd "to hammer to death those scum, those scum who have decided to go ahead with introducing new fascism", as well as suggesting that the offices of MPs who had voted for the restrictions should be burned down. [[Home Secretary]] [[Priti Patel]] responded to online footage of Corbyn's speech, describing it as "sickening" and called for the police to take action against him.<ref>{{cite news|title=Home Sec hits out at 'sickening' clip of Piers Corbyn telling people to 'hammer MPs to death'|url=https://www.lbc.co.uk/politics/priti-patel-piers-corbyn-sickening-clip/|work=LBC|date=18 December 2021|access-date=18 December 2021}}</ref> On 19 December, Corbyn was arrested for his comments.<ref name=":0">{{cite news|last=Wolfe-Robinson|first=Maya|date=19 December 2021|title=Piers Corbyn arrested on suspicion of calling for MPs' offices to be burned down|newspaper=The Guardian|url=https://theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/dec/19/piers-corbyn-arrested-on-suspicion-of-calling-for-mps-offices-to-be-burned-down}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Piers Corbyn arrested over video calling for people to 'burn down the offices of MPs'|url=https://news.sky.com/story/piers-corbyn-arrested-over-video-calling-for-people-to-burn-down-the-offices-of-mps-12499698|access-date=20 December 2021|website=Sky News|language=en}}</ref>{{needs update|date=January 2025}}
